title: where constraints
sub: class, struct, new(), unmanaged and interfaces
cards/0/title: What you can require of T
cards/0/body:
class — a reference type (can be null).
struct — a value type.
unmanaged — a value type with no references inside (works with stackalloc and pointers).
new() — has a public parameterless constructor.
An interface — T has its methods.
cards/1/task: A factory creates a new object of type T. It must work with List<int> and Point.
cards/2/options/0: string has no public parameterless constructor
cards/2/explain: new string() does not compile — so string does not satisfy new() either.
cards/3/task: A cache holds a T value and can reset it to null. It must work with string and List<int>, but not with int.
cards/4/task: A fast stack buffer via stackalloc. It must work with int and Point.
cards/5/body: class and struct can't be combined. unmanaged already means "value type", so you don't write it with struct, class or new(). Order: class/struct/unmanaged first, then interfaces, new() last.
cards/6/explain: new() always goes at the end of the list.
cards/7/q: What does default(T) return for T = int and T = string?
cards/7/explain: default means "zeros": the zero value for value types, null for reference types.
cards/8/q: Match the constraint to what it allows
cards/9/q: Which types satisfy where T : struct? Select all.
cards/9/explain: string is a reference type. int? is Nullable<int>: it is a value type, but the struct constraint deliberately rejects it.
